Exec.description: A process started in a sandbox. It keeps running when clients disconnect. Execs live as long as their sandbox.

exit_code.description: Set once `exited`. A process killed by a signal reports 128 + the signal number (e.g. 137 for SIGKILL).

timeout.description: Exec timeout in seconds, if set.

workdir.description: Working directory: the one given, else the sandbox's. `null` when neither is known: the sandbox was created without `workdir` and its image's wasn't read.

ExecCreateReq.description: A command to run in a running sandbox.

command.description: Argv to run, e.g. `["python", "train.py"]`: at most 4096 arguments, each at most 131071 bytes in UTF-8, at most 1 MiB in total, with no NUL byte (else `invalid_command`).

env.description: Extra environment variables on top of the sandbox's environment. Same rules as on create: POSIX names, no `TELNYX_SANDBOX_` prefix, size limits (else `invalid_env`).

timeout.description: Stop the process after this many seconds (status `terminated`, reason `timeout`). Default: no limit. At most 2147483647 (about 68 years); it never outlives the sandbox.

workdir.description: Absolute working directory (else `invalid_workdir`). Defaults to the sandbox's working directory.

ExecStatus.description: `starting` → `running` → `exited`. `failed`: the process was never confirmed started (see `reason`: `sandbox_terminated`, `agent_unavailable`, `cancelled` or `agent_error`). An `agent_unavailable` or `cancelled` exec can still move on to `running`, `exited` or `terminated` if its start did reach the sandbox. `terminated`: the process was stopped because the sandbox ended or the exec's `timeout` was reached.

Signal.description: Signal to send, as an uppercase POSIX signal name.

url.description: Documentation page for the error code.

TelnyxErrorSource.description: Where in the request the error was found.

pointer.description: JSON pointer into the request body, e.g. `/timeout`.

total_results.description: Number of items across all pages.

sandboxes_TelnyxError.description: One error in the standard Telnyx error body.

code.description: Telnyx error code: a 5-digit string for general errors, e.g. `10009`. Sandboxes-specific errors are identified by their name in `title`.

title.description: Short, constant summary of the error. For Sandboxes-specific errors, the error's name, e.g. `quota_exceeded`.

BearerAuth.description: Telnyx API key supplied as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. In production, auth may be validated by the API gateway and forwarded via Telnyx auth headers.

Payment.description: Machine Payment Protocol credential used on paid retries, sent as `Authorization: Payment ...`. Obtained by paying a challenge returned in the `WWW-Authenticate` header of a 402 response. This is not a Telnyx API key; initial challenge requests use standard bearer authentication instead.

post.description:
Starts a command inside a running sandbox and returns the exec at once: `running`, or `exited` with its `exit_code` if it already finished. It doesn't wait for the command or stream its output: attach to the exec's WebSocket for its output and stdin, or wait for the exit code with `GET /ai/sandboxes/{sandbox_id}/execs/{exec_id}?wait=…`.

If the sandbox can't confirm the start within a few seconds (it may still be starting up), the exec comes back `starting`, and the start completes in the background: follow it with `GET /ai/sandboxes/{sandbox_id}/execs/{exec_id}`. A start that can't be confirmed within 5 minutes ends `failed` with reason `agent_unavailable`.

The process keeps running when you disconnect. It uses the sandbox's working directory and environment unless you override them.

Send an `Idempotency-Key`: a retry with the same key returns the same exec instead of starting the command twice, and completes a start that was still `starting`.

parameters.description: Optional client-chosen key (e.g. a UUID, at most 255 characters) that makes the call safe to retry. Within 24 h, the same key with the same request returns the stored response instead of acting twice; the same key with a different request fails with `idempotency_key_reused`; a request with a key that's still being processed fails with `request_in_progress`.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

get.description: Returns the exec: `status`, `exit_code` and `reason`. With `wait`, it's a long-poll: it returns as soon as the exec has ended, or after at most 10 s, always with `200`; call again until `status` is `exited`, `failed` or `terminated`. If the sandbox can't answer, you get the last known state.

parameters.description: Seconds to wait for the exec to end. `0` (default) returns at once; the server waits at most 10 s and clamps larger values.

post.description:
Sends a signal to the exec's process group (default `SIGKILL`). It's asynchronous: the response shows the exec as it is right after; with `SIGKILL` it ends shortly after with `status` `exited` and `exit_code` 137 (128 + the signal number). Signalling an exec that already ended changes nothing.

An exec still `starting` can only be cancelled: `SIGKILL` makes sure the command never runs (it ends `failed` with reason `cancelled`); another signal gets `exec_not_started`. Retry once it's `running`.

With an `Idempotency-Key`, a retry replays the first answer. Two overlapping requests with the same key may both deliver the signal.

parameters.description: Optional client-chosen key (e.g. a UUID, at most 255 characters) that makes the call safe to retry. Within 24 h, the same key with the same request returns the stored response instead of acting twice; the same key with a different request fails with `idempotency_key_reused`; a request with a key that's still being processed fails with `request_in_progress`.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

post.description:
Sends EOF to the exec's stdin, as the exec attach WebSocket's `stdin_eof` message does: the process sees it once the input already accepted has been written. Disconnecting never sends EOF; a process reading stdin keeps waiting until you call this. Closing it twice, or on an exec that ended, changes nothing.

An exec still `starting` is started first. While your organization's sandboxes are disabled, that's refused with `sandboxes_disabled`.

parameters.description: Optional client-chosen key (e.g. a UUID, at most 255 characters) that makes the call safe to retry.
